The problem asks to identify a guaranteed identity involving multiple zeta values (MZVs) of a specific structure. The MZV is defined as:
$$\zeta(k_1,\dots,k_r)=\sum_{n_1>\cdots>n_r\ge 1} n_1^{-k_1}\cdots n_r^{-k_r}$$
Here, $\{2\}^m$ denotes a string of $m$ copies of $2$. The arguments are positive integers. Since $a, b, c$ are positive integers, we need to check the constraints on the lengths of the strings.

The structure of the left-hand side (LHS) is $\zeta(\{2\}^{a-1},3,\{2\}^{c-1},1,\{2\}^b)$.
For this to be well-defined, the arguments must be positive integers.
1. $a-1 \ge 0$, so $a \ge 1$. (Given $a$ is a positive integer)
2. $3 \ge 1$. (True)
3. $c-1 \ge 0$, so $c \ge 1$. (Given $c$ is a positive integer)
4. $1 \ge 1$. (True)
5. $b \ge 1$. (Given $b$ is a positive integer)
